sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier mandibles relatively slender, the mandibular teeth small and angular, the vertex raised; on these characters it is distinguished from the other species of the genus.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Not recorded in the original (Not known).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head ochraceous orange, antennae yellow ochraceous, mandibles pale rusty. Head short, broad and very deep, slightly wider in the middle, the posterior margin almost truncate; in profile the frons rises at a fairly steep angle to a very prominent vertex and then descends steeply to the posterior margin. Mandibles long, slender and strongly curved, the teeth very small, situated slightly nearer the apex than the base. Postmentum very narrow (width 0.22), the sides nearly parallel, distinctly convex. Labrum rather small, about as long as wide, the apex conical. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 smallest. Measurements: total length 5.25 mm, head length (mandibles crossed, including mandibles) 2.22 mm, head length (to apex of labrum) 1.66—1.70 mm, head width 1.25—1.32 mm, pronotum length 0.33—0.37 mm, width 0.70 mm.

note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), originally in English; the original describes only the soldier, the alate is recorded as Not known, and the worker is known only as a morphotype without description, so no worker section is given. The synonymy notes that the species was originally described by Hill in 1933 as Ramitermes capito in Coun. Sci. Ind. Res. (Aust.) Pamph. no. 52, p. 29 (the list gives Hill, 1935; doubtful, pending verification). OCR problems: the genus name appears as Hcmitermes, the species heading as "capito Hill" while the text figure caption reads Hcmitermes; the angle of the frons is OCR'd as "k3°" (probably 43°) and was not used to rewrite the text; "3nd" is an error for 3rd; "G-ula" is gula (postmentum). Distribution and biology are not translated into the morphology section.
